{{Short description|Polish geophysicist, seismologist, and academic (1951–2020)}}
{{Orphan|date=December 2020}}

'''Marek Andrzej Grad''' (November 19, 1951 – May 17, 2020<ref>{{cite web | title= With regret we inform you | url= https://www.igf.fuw.edu.pl/en/articles/aktualnosci-y/z-wielkim-smutkiem-zawiadamiam-32020-05-18/ | publisher = Institute of Geophysics, University of Warsaw | date=2020-05-18| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20210304202728/https://www.igf.fuw.edu.pl/en/articles/aktualnosci-y/z-wielkim-smutkiem-zawiadamiam-32020-05-18/ | archive-date= 2021-03-04 }}</ref>) was a Polish [[Geophysics|geophysicist]] and seismologist, and a professor of Earth sciences. He worked in the Department of Physics of Litosphere of the Institute of Geophysics at the [[University of Warsaw]].

In the years 1991-2002 he was the director of the Institute of Geophysics of the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw. In the years 2012-2014 dean of the Division III [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] (Science and Earth Sciences). From 2014 he has been a member of the board of curators of this faculty. A foreign member of the [[Finnish Academy of Science and Letters|Finnish Academy of Sciences]], he was a member of the steering committee of the [[NATO]] Science for Peace program

The scientific activity of Marek Grad was [[seismology]], especially structural seismology. He studied the Earth's crust and the upper mantle using the methods of explosive seismology (mainly the so-called deep seismic sounding). He participated in research in Finland, [[Spitsbergen]] and West Antarctica, among others.<ref>{{cite web| title=Marek Grad/lecture| url = https://zapytajfizyka.fuw.edu.pl/wyklady/marek-grad/}}</ref> He was the creator of the digital map of [[Mohorovičić discontinuity]] for the European Plate. This was the first map that shows the depth of Mohorovičić discontinuity for the whole of Europe.<ref>{{cite web|title=How deep is Moho?| url=https://forumakademickie.pl/fa-archiwum/archiwum/2009/04/30_jak_gleboko_jest_moho.html}}</ref> He was the coordinator of such physical experiments as POLONAISE'97, CELEBRATION 2000, ALP 2002, [[Sudetes|SUDETES]] 2003, TOR, PASSEQ 2006-2008 and 13 BB-STAR.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marek Grad|url=http://tedxlazarskiuniversity.eu/2018/05/24/marek-grad-2/|access-date=2019-07-02|archive-date=2018-10-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025070945/http://tedxlazarskiuniversity.eu/2018/05/24/marek-grad-2/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also popularized science.
